R0271.title: VLA/VLM Model Adversarial Attack
R0271.definition: Adversarial-example, adversarial-patch, jailbreak, and cross-modal injection attacks against Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and Vision-Language Models (VLM) that make the model output wrong action sequences or perform forbidden actions.
R0271.description:
VLA/VLM model adversarial attack is the core model-layer threat of embodied intelligence. RoboPAIR is the first jailbreak algorithm against LLM-controlled robots, achieving often 100% attack success on white-box NVIDIA Dolphins autonomous-driving LLM, gray-box Clearpath Jackal UGV, and black-box Unitree Go2+GPT-3.5, inducing weaponization, collision, and other harmful physical behaviors. BadRobot jailbreaks embodied LLMs via voice interaction to violate safety/ethics constraints. UPA-RFAS (CVPR 2026) proposes a single adversarial patch with black-box cross-model transfer, dropping task success by up to 100%. VLA-Attacker implements spatially-grounded untargeted/targeted attacks. These attacks make sorting robots grab wrong materials, service robots hand wrong items, and autonomous vehicles misjudge obstacles.

This risk belongs to the VLA model-layer attack family together with R0267 (physical-world prompt injection) and R0274 (cross-modal injection); this risk focuses on digital adversarial examples and jailbreaks, R0267 on physical-environment injectioncarrier, and R0274 on cross-modal manipulation.
R0271.influence: Causes robots to perform wrong or dangerous actions, model capabilities to be abused, and safety alignment to be bypassed; it is a core model-layer risk distinguishing embodied intelligence from traditional robots, directly translatable into physical-world harm.
